1: A young man of good family in Sāvatthī heard the Buddha teach at Jetavana. Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, he went forth as a monk.
2: After five years, having learned by heart the monks’ and nuns’ codes of discipline, he received a meditation subject that suited his temperament and went into the forest.
3: He strove through the three months of the Rains but could not raise even a glimmer of a sign. Thinking, “There is no path or fruit for me in this life,” he went back to Jetavana.
4:
His fellow monks brought him, unwilling, to the Buddha, who said,
“Once your effort found water in the desert and saved everyone; why give up effort now?”
Then the monks asked him to tell that story.
5: Long ago, when Brahmadatta reigned in Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was a caravan leader. He set out with five hundred carts.
6: They entered a sixty-yojana desert. The sand was so fine that it would not stay in a closed fist.
7: Once the sun rose, the sand grew as hot as glowing coals. By day they set the carts in a circle and rested under awnings.
8:
The fine sand held no landmarks. At sunset they travelled on,
and a land-pilot on the front cart found the way by the stars.
9: After fifty-nine yojanas they thought one more night would bring them out of the desert, so they threw away the rest of their water and firewood.
10:
That night the pilot, worn out from many sleepless nights, fell asleep.
The oxen turned around and went back the way they had come.
11: Without anyone noticing, the carts went back along the road all through the night.
12: At dawn the pilot woke and shouted, “Turn the carts around!” But they were at the very place where they had camped the day before.
13: With no water and no firewood, the men lay under the carts and wept. The Bodhisatta thought, “If I give up, everyone will die.”
14:
In the cool of the dawn the Bodhisatta saw a clump of dabba grass.
“It grows from moisture below; there must be water under it,” he thought.
15: He had hoes brought and told the men to dig there. They dug down sixty cubits.
16: But when the hoes struck rock, all the men gave up.
17: The Bodhisatta went down into the pit and put his ear to the rock. He heard the sound of water flowing beneath it.
18:
He called the young servant who had not given up and said, “If you give up, we will all die.”
He gave him an iron hammer and told him to go down and strike the rock.
19: All the others had given up, but the young servant did not give up. He struck the rock.
20:
The rock that had blocked the water split in two,
and a column of water as big as a palm trunk rose up.
21: Everyone drank and bathed. They split spare axles and yokes for firewood, cooked rice, and fed the oxen too.
22: At sunset they raised a flag beside the well and set out once more.
23:
They reached their destination, made two, three and four times their money,
and came home safely.
24:
“The young servant then is this monk who gave up his effort,
and the caravan leader was I myself.” That monk attained arahantship.
